events.title: Utah Conference on Undergraduate Research Accepting Proposals
events.description:
The Utah Conference on Undergraduate Research (UCUR) is for all undergraduate students doing research in the state of Utah, and it rotates which university hosts the conference each year. Utah State University will be hosting this year on February 26, 2027.

Undergraduates from all disciplines are invited to apply for the conference, which provides an excellent opportunity for students to present their work in a scholarly setting to students, faculty, field specialists, and community members. Presentations may include both visual and oral displays of work in all academic disciplines, from art history to molecular biology as well as performance of creative research within the visual and performing arts.

BYU will pay the conference registration fee and provide transportation to/from USU for all students presenting at the conference.

Applications are currently being accepted and the deadline for submissions is November 2, 2026.

Visit research.usu.edu to apply and get more information.

Contact adrienne.jensen@byu.edu or at 801-422-5995.

events.title: Devotional: Bishop L. Todd Budge
events.description:
Bishop L. Todd Budge was named First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric on November 14, 2025. Bishop Budge was sustained as a General Authority Seventy on April 6, 2019, and served in that capacity until his call as Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric in October 2020. Bishop Budge has served in a number of Church callings, including stake president, president of the Japan Tokyo Mission, and Area Seventy.

Bishop Budge received a bachelor of arts degree in economics from BYU in 1984. He worked for Bain & Company Japan; Citibank, N.A.; and GE Capital in both Atlanta and Japan. In 2003 he became president and chief executive officer of Tokyo Star Bank Limited; from 2008 to 2011 he served as chairman of the board. He retired from the bank in 2011. During this time, he also served as a member of the board of directors for Hawaiian Airlines.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: The Kingdom of Heaven's Long March: Christianity and the Public Sphere in Modern China
events.description:
From Jesuit efforts to woo the Ming and Qing dynasties’ imperial courts and scholar-officials, to the early twentieth century Protestant educationalists promotion of the modernization of state and society, and on to recent cases of the house churches sometimes contentious relations with the communist government, Christians in China have regularly advocated for varying degrees of freedom for themselves and for others. By examining a few key moments in the history of the Church in China, as well as the challenges posed by secular nationalism, this talk examines the role Christians have played in developing a public sphere a China.

Jeff Kyong-McClain is an associate professor of history and the director of the Habib Institute for Asian Studies at the University of Idaho. His research interests include the history of missions and higher education in China. Recently, he co-edited From Missionary Education to Confucius Institutes: Historical Reflections on Sino-American Cultural Exchange and is a co-organizer of “Crossing Boundaries and Christianity in the Sinophone World,” a conference to be held at Hong Kong Baptist University this December.

Part of the Kennedy Center's fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."

events.title: Dressed to Rule: French Fashion & Feminine Power from Marie Antoinette to the Belle Époque
events.description:
In “Dressed to Rule,” Caroline Weber presents two women of privilege in France—Queen Marie Antoinette in the late 18th century, and the Countess Greffulhe, the acknolwedged queen of aristocratic Parisian society, in the 19th century—who used clothing as a singularly potent form of self-expression and self-empowerment. Weber is interested in how both women turned to fashion to assert their agency and enhance their authority in a male-dominated society in crisis: pre-revolutionary and revolutionary France in Marie Antoinette’s case, and the French Third Republic in Mme Greffulhe’s case.

Caroline Weber is Professor of French and Comparative Literature at Barnard College, where she specializes in the literature and history of the French ancien régime, Enlightenment, and Revolution.

Part of the Global Women's Studies Colloquium.

events.title: The Wonder of Scripture with Spencer Fluhman
events.description:
Spencer Fluhman will deliver this Wonder of Scripture lecture. He is an associate professor and chair of the Department of History at Brigham Young University, where he focuses on religious history, Latter-day Saint history, American religion, and North America from 1800 to 1914. Fluhman is known for his leadership as executive director of the Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship from 2016 to 2023 and for scholarship recognized by the Mormon History Association.

The Wonder of Scripture series, sponsored by BYU’s Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, invites speakers from diverse backgrounds to explore how sacred texts shape understanding, inspire wonder, and inform meaningful lives. Each lecture offers a distinctive perspective on scripture and its enduring significance.

The keynote speaker will be Professor Ashutosh Varshney, Brown University Professor of Political Science and Sol Goldman Professor of International Studies and the Social Sciences. His remarks will be titled "India's Democratic Backsliding: A Theoretical and Comparative Perspective."

Other presenters include Robert Colson, David Romney, Evan Ward, Shad Morris, Brandon Webb, and Michael Easterling.

Sponsored by the Asian Studies program at the Kennedy Center for International Studies.

Join BYUradio for a free screening of A House United, a documentary featuring stories of people bridging differences in our deeply divided world.

Have you ever felt worn out by the heat in our public conversations—or wondered if there’s a way out of all this division? A House United is a new 60-minute documentary made in partnership with BYU Broadcasting that offers a hopeful answer. Through inspiring stories of people building bridges across political and social divides, the film shows what can happen when we listen, find common ground, and choose to work together.

Join us for a brief Q&A, plus refreshments, following the screening.

events.title: Utah Conference on Undergraduate Research Proposals Due
events.description:
The Utah Conference on Undergraduate Research (UCUR) is for all undergraduate students doing research in the state of Utah, and it rotates which university hosts the conference each year. Utah State University will be hosting this year on February 26, 2027.

Undergraduates from all disciplines are invited to apply for the conference, which provides an excellent opportunity for students to present their work in a scholarly setting to students, faculty, field specialists, and community members. Presentations may include both visual and oral displays of work in all academic disciplines, from art history to molecular biology as well as performance of creative research within the visual and performing arts.

BYU will pay the conference registration fee and provide transportation to/from USU for all students presenting at the conference.

Applications are currently being accepted and the deadline for submissions is November 2, 2026.

Visit research.usu.edu to apply and get more information.

Contact adrienne.jensen@byu.edu or at 801-422-5995.

events.title: Devotional: Audrey Perry Martin
events.description:
Audrey Perry Martin was appointed assistant to the president for University Communications on June 1, 2025. In this role, she acts as the university’s primary spokesperson and directs the work of BYU University Communications. Perry Martin earned a law degree from Georgetown University Law Center and a bachelor’s degree in political science and journalism from BYU.

Prior to her current role, Perry Martin was a partner at Lex Politica, a national political law firm. Her practice focused on advising corporations, candidates, political committees and parties on campaign and election law issues. Additionally, she worked as counsel for the Committee on House Administration and at the Federal Election Commission.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Joni L. Koch
events.description:
Elder Joni L. Koch was sustained as a General Authority Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 1, 2017. At the time of his call, he had been serving as president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission. He previously served as Second Counselor in the Africa Southeast Area Presidency and President of the Brazil Area. He currently serves in the United States Northeast Area. Elder Koch has served in numerous Church callings, including stake president, Area Seventy and president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission.

Elder Koch received a Bachelor of Science degree in statistics from BYU in 1991. He received an executive MBA from FGV/SP in 1994. During his career he has worked in senior management positions at Cargill Foods, AP Moller Maersk Group, and was the CEO of CM Ltd. at the time of his call as mission president.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: Jamie Jensen will present the 2026 Alice Louise Reynolds Women in Scholarship Lecture
events.description:
EVOLVING UNDERSTANDING: A JOURNEY THROUGH EVOLUTION, RELIGION, AND THE ART OF COMMUNICATION

Dr. Jensen, a Professor at the BYU School of Medicine, will trace the intellectually illuminating and at times challenging journey she has taken through her research into how people learn about and come to accept—or resist-evolutionary theory within a faith community. She will discuss her research findings as well as the personal insights she has gained about communicating across ideological divides. Ultimately, this journey has strengthened both her faith in God and her conviction that science and faith can serve as complementary and mutually enriching ways of seeking

The unselfish touch of Alice Louise Reynolds can still be felt at Brigham Young University. The Harold B. Lee Library can trace its beginnings to a committee on which Miss Reynolds served, first as a member and later as chair. She devoted many years to building the dream of a large and comprehensive university library at BYU. Today the Harold B. Lee Library stands as a monument to her dedication and vision.

This lecture series has been established to honor Alice Louise Reynolds and to feature women in scholarship. It is through the generosity of members of the Alice Louise Reynolds Clubs and other Friends of the Library that the endowment for this annual lectureship has been made possible.

events.title: Forum: Anne Snyder
events.description:
Anne Snyder is the editor-in-chief of Comment, a magazine of public theology for the common good and a growing ecosystem of conversation and moral imagination rooted in the Christian humanist tradition. She is also the creator and host of the Understory, Comment’s three-day “living magazine” and cultural festival, which debuted at Washington National Cathedral in 2026.

Anne is the author of The Fabric of Character: A Wise Giver’s Guide to Renewing Our Social and Moral Landscape and the creator of Breaking Ground, a collaborative publishing project and network of institutions that later became the book Breaking Ground: Charting Our Future in a Pandemic Year. Previously, she directed The Philanthropy Roundtable’s Character Initiative. She is a Senior Fellow of The Trinity Forum and lives in Washington, D.C.

events.title: The Hebrew Bible's Ancient Avengers
events.description:
Long before Spider-Man, Wonder Woman, Batman and the Guardians of the Galaxy, the Hebrew Bible’s Ancient Avengers were inspiring Americans. Ripped from the story from ancient Israel, the figures of Samson, Esther, Elijah, and David served as spiritual sustenance to freedom fighters, politicians, and pundits striving to see the United States live up to its founding ideals. In this lecture we will examine how these Hebraic heroes shaped the American story from its founding era to today.

Rabbi Dr. Stuart Halpern serves as the senior advisor to the provost as well as the deputy director and chief strategy officer of the Zahava and Moshael J. Straus Center for Torah and Western Thought at Yeshiva University. In addition to his doctorate in education, Rabbi Halpern has master’s degrees in both Bible and Psychology in Education, and an MBA in Nonprofit Management.

events.title: The Wonder of Scripture with Kimberly Matheson
events.description:
Kimberly Matheson will deliver this Wonder of Scripture lecture. She is the Laura F. Willes Research Fellow at the Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship at Brigham Young University, where she focuses on Book of Mormon theology, Christian contemplative practice, and the continental philosophy of religion. Matheson is known for authoring Helaman: A Brief Theological Introduction and for her service on the boards of the Book of Mormon Studies Association and the Latter-day Saint Theology Seminar.

The Wonder of Scripture series, sponsored by BYU’s Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, invites speakers from diverse backgrounds to explore how sacred texts shape understanding, inspire wonder, and inform meaningful lives. Each lecture offers a distinctive perspective on scripture and its enduring significance.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
events.description:
Elder Gerrit W. Gong currently serves as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He previously served as a member of the Asia Area Presidency and member of the Presidency of the Seventy.

During his 20 years in Washington, D.C., he served as special assistant to the undersecretary of state at the U.S. State Department, as special assistant to the U.S. ambassador in Beijing, China, and in several positions at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C. He was also assistant to the president for planning and assessment at BYU.

Elder Gong holds a doctorate in international relations and a master’s degree in philosophy from Oxford University, where he was a Rhodes scholar. He also holds a bachelor's degree in Asian and university studies from BYU.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

Let your creativity soar as you use colorful buttons to make your own décor and allow your inner child to come out and play! Free supplies and admission included at the Education in Zion Gallery. 

Disclaimer: Researchers agree, taking short breaks and working with your hands may give your brain a rest, improve later studying, and enhance your understanding of the four aims of a BYU education. (Okay, this last one didn’t show up in an official study . . . yet!) 

Go to the top of the spiral staircase in the JFSB and follow the signs to the craft room. These crafts take about 20 minutes or less and all supplies are FREE. 4 to 8 pm. We look forward to creating with you!

events.title: Feathered Creatures with Purbayan Chatterjee & Mark Lettieri
events.description:
This boundary-expanding performance from Grammy-winning guitarist Mark Lettieri and sitar virtuoso Purbayan Chatterjee brings to life the sound-world of their collaborative album of the same name. Rooted in Indian classical tradition and modern jazz and rock, Feathered Creatures both honors the past and soars into the future. East and West meet not as opposites but as partners, dissolving borders between tradition and innovation.

CONCERT HALL (MB)
$12-47

events.title: The Diary of Anne Frank
events.description:
It’s Amsterdam, 1942, and as the Frank family goes into hiding to avoid being deported with other Jews, silence is the rule. Thirteen-year old Anne’s personality is too big for her cramped hiding place. Fortunately, in her diary she has full freedom of expression. Anne’s words stretch beyond the limits of her time, place, and life. This firsthand account of family and friendship in dark times is an anthem to the human spirit.

You are invited to attend the Student Innovator of the Year (SIOY) Competition Kickoff on Thursday, Sep. 10, 6-7 PM in the Engineering Building Event Space (EB 204/206) to learn more about the competition.
 
 There will be pizza and giveaways of products invented by past SIOY competitors: Phone Soap UV Light Phone Sanitizer/Charger, MyoStorm vibrating massage therapy ball, and Klymit hammock.
 We'll also be hosting an ideation activity at Kickoff!

events.title: Baylor New Venture Competition Submission Deadline
events.description:
link: https://hankamer.baylor.edu/baugh-center/new-venture
description: Pitch competition open to all collegiate entrepreneurs. Teams receive executive summary feedback, business plan coaching, one-on-one mentorship, and multiple rounds of pitch feedback throughout the competition cycle. Teams compete for more than $200,000 in cash and in-kind prizes. Don't miss out on this opportunity! Apply early.

events.title: Creators Club Kickoff
events.description:
Got a business idea? Come find out how to actually get it off the ground.

Join us for the Creators Club kickoff event — a one-hour intro to what Creators Club is all about, what we do, and what's coming this semester, including the Big Idea Competition. We'll also have free food from Sage, Andy Gartz's restaurant in Provo. Before we wrap up, we'll ask you to fill out a quick feedback survey so we can build a semester around what you're most excited to learn.

Here's what to expect after kickoff: every week, a different student speaker will share a real business story in a quick, 10-minute case study — walking through how they took an idea from nothing (level 0) to something real (level 1) through validation. This semester is all about validation — testing your idea before you sink time and money into it. You'll hear directly from students who've used Rollins Center resources, including the Validation Grant, to get their own ideas off the ground.

And here's the fun part: if you make a sale from your business anytime this semester, you're invited to an exclusive end-of-semester dinner — gourmet pizza, made by Sage.

events.title: Utah Entrepreneur Challenge Application Deadline
events.description:
The Tim Draper Utah Entrepreneur Challenge (UEC) is a statewide, student business competition. Teams from universities across Utah compete for the best student business and a chance to win cash and prizes. We invite all students in Utah from participating colleges and universities to apply. The challenge will culminate with at a final event at the University of Utah. Participating teams are judged by industry professionals, experienced entrepreneurs and community experts. Judges will allocate $75,000 in prizes and awards to the top 20 finalists. Many past winners have developed into successful enterprises. The program is managed by the Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute at the University of Utah. Sponsors include Tim Draper, a renowned venture capitalist.

https://lassonde.utah.edu/uec/apply/

events.title: College Lecture
events.description:
D. Brett Pennington (BS '94) is a senior energy executive with nearly 30 years of leadership and technical experience in the oil and gas industry. He currently serves as President and Chief Executive Officer of Ensign Natural Resources, a private equity-backed exploration and production company focused on the acquisition, development and optimization of oil and gas assets. Under his leadership, Ensign acquired a 130,000-acre position and built a management and operating organization of over 140 employees. The company transformed the asset in just three years before selling to Marathon Oil for approximately $3 billion.

Prior to Ensign, Mr. Pennington held senior executive positions with Murphy Oil Corporation and spent more than a decade with ExxonMobil in engineering, planning, project management, and leadership roles. Mr. Pennington serves on the Board of Directors of the Texas Oil & Gas Association. He holds a bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering from Brigham Young University and completed the Advanced Management Program at Harvard Business School, along with executive programs at Wharton and Thunderbird.

events.title: Weekly Seminar - Kendell Clement
events.description:
Abstract
CRISPR genome editing has transformed biology by making it possible to alter DNA at precisely chosen locations. It is now a powerful research tool for testing how genes work and a growing therapeutic platform for personalized treatments for disease. However, realizing CRISPR’s potential depends on computational methods that can accurately measure editing outcomes, identify meaningful biological consequences, and guide the design of increasingly complex edits.
In this talk, I will share how computer science and bioinformatics can advance CRISPR research and therapeutic development. I will describe my work on CRISPResso2, an alignment-based software tool for interpreting sequencing data from genome-editing experiments. I will then discuss how CRISPR screens can model and study disease-associated mutations. Finally, I will look ahead to computational challenges in analyzing coordinated editing at multiple genomic targets for next-generation CAR T-cell therapies. Together, these examples illustrate how algorithms and biological experiments work together to make genome editing more precise, interpretable, and clinically useful.
Biography
Dr. Kendell Clement, PhD is an assistant professor in the Department of Biomedical Informatics at the University of Utah. He received a BS in Computer Science and Bioinformatics from Brigham Young University and was a Fulbright scholar at the Free University in Berlin. He completed a PhD in Medical Engineering from MIT and Harvard where he studied epigenetic changes in development and disease, particularly dysregulation of DNA methylation in blood cancers. He pursued postdoctoral research studies at the Massachusetts General Hospital where he developed software for analyzing genome editing experiments and collaborated with other groups in the development of next-generation genome editing tools such as base editors. Currently, his group is interested in developing new computational tools and everaging cutting-edge experimental technologies to understand the genetics and epigenetics of disease
initiation.

events.title: The Kingdom of Heaven's Long March: Christianity and the Public Sphere in Modern China
events.description:
From Jesuit efforts to woo the Ming and Qing dynasties’ imperial courts and scholar-officials, to the early twentieth century Protestant educationalists promotion of the modernization of state and society, and on to recent cases of the house churches sometimes contentious relations with the communist government, Christians in China have regularly advocated for varying degrees of freedom for themselves and for others. By examining a few key moments in the history of the Church in China, as well as the challenges posed by secular nationalism, this talk examines the role Christians have played in developing a public sphere a China.
Jeff Kyong-McClain is an associate professor of history and the director of the Habib Institute for Asian Studies at the University of Idaho. His research interests include the history of missions and higher education in China. Recently, he co-edited From Missionary Education to Confucius Institutes: Historical Reflections on Sino-American Cultural Exchange and is a co-organizer of “Crossing Boundaries and Christianity in the Sinophone World,” a conference to be held at Hong Kong Baptist University this December.
Part of our fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."

events.title: Lunch and Learn: Are Buildings Parasites?
events.description:
Buildings provide shelter, but they also consume significant resources and can even deplete those available in their surrounding communities. But what if instead they could leave the environment better off than they found it?
Bring your lunch and join Dr. Kieren McCord to discuss indoor environmental quality and whole-building life cycle assessment, exploring the impacts buildings have from initial design through the end of their useful life.
This event will happen in the Stewardship Lab, 139 SCOB (450 E 700 N in Provo).
Sponsored by the Kennedy Center's Global Environmental Studies program.
Event Flyer

events.title: Dressed to Rule: French Fashion & Feminine Power from Marie Antoinette to the Belle Époque
events.description:
In “Dressed to Rule,” Caroline Weber presents two women of privilege in France—Queen Marie Antoinette in the late 18th century, and the Countess Greffulhe, the acknolwedged queen of aristocratic Parisian society, in the 19th century—who used clothing as a singularly potent form of self-expression and self-empowerment. Weber is interested in how both women turned to fashion to assert their agency and enhance their authority in a male-dominated society in crisis: pre-revolutionary and revolutionary France in Marie Antoinette’s case, and the French Third Republic in Mme Greffulhe’s case.
Caroline Weber is Professor of French and Comparative Literature at Barnard College, where she specializes in the literature and history of the French ancien régime, Enlightenment, and Revolution.
Part of the Global Women's Studies Colloquium.

Stop in anytime from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, except during devotionals (Tuesdays 11:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.). Come and serve whenever you can for however long you can!
